data.name: 摩尼遊戯TOKOYO
data.detailed_description:
mani yugi TOKOYO is a pixel art shooting game inspired by the Japanese Buddhist worldview. In it, players become a priest who gets into a mokugyo (a Buddhist temple block) and goes on a journey around the Rokudo. Players can choose from six stages, Tendo (heaven), Ningendo (human world), Chikshodo (animal world), Jigokudo (hell), Gakido (hungry world), and Syurado (fighting world), where they save wandering souls using the power of "Yoshi Yoshi" (there there) launched from the mokugyo. The goal of each stage is to reach the Kannon waiting for you at the end.The game also includes collectable elements, where delivered souls are gathered around the temple.
The purpose of this game is to reach its final stage, TOKOYO (the place of the truth).

reviews.review:
[url=http://store.steampowered.com/curator/32482033/]Crim's Humble Opinion Curator[/url]

[h1]Perseverance Is Key[/h1]
Maniyugi TOKOYO is a relentlessly hard shoot em up set in world that uses a journey around the Rokudo in order to reach the place of truth to find your enlightment. This game got an english translation so the lore and mechanics are much more accessible to players who don't understand the original language. One of the first things I recognized in this game that brought me back was the ability to switch worlds. I instantly thought of the game Ikaruga with it's color switching mechanic and in this game you will have to master the switching mechanic to survive. There are six main stages followed by a final stage and final boss. You can play the first six stages in any order but have to play the last two in order. During each stage you can either be killed by running out of inspiration or getting knocked off screen by moving blocks. The blocks is where you will have to use your switch because each block exists on one plane but not the other. The influence loss on hits is pretty forgiving but the blocks are where you will get relentless one hit deaths. At the end of each stage you face a boss and have to utilize both planes in order to knock down two health bars (one for each plane). The soundtrack is pretty awesome and the theme and art is really cool. It's also just great to see a game that isn't normally widely available more accessible to different audiences. 

[h1]The Minor Gripes[/h1]
This game is super difficult especially towards the end. I don't know if I will be able to personally clear it but I don't really see the difficulty as something I can gripe at since the genre is known to have insane difficulties. The issues I have with this game are just really minor things mostly to do with porting and option access. There aren't really any tweaking options. There also isn't a real way to close the game without alt tabbing out and closing it. I've ran into a few softlock freezes in the overworld that cause me to have to reboot the game. Some of the dialogue progression in the hub world can be a bit slow. Other than these mostly minor issues I don't have anything else bad to say. 

[code][h1](っ◔◡◔)っ ♥ pros ♥[/h1]
+More accessible to players since initial release
+Awesome Music
+Interesting mechanics

[h1](っ>▬<)っ x cons x[/h1]
-Minor lack of user interface and options 
-Some soft locks 
[/code]

While this is really cool I can recommend this mostly and only to fans of bullet hell and hard shoot em up titles such as the touhou games or ikaruga. This is one of those games that can be fairly short if you are really good at them or can be really long if you like to replay it for score chasing and enjoyment. Either way the game will probably seem to have a higher quality of life with a sale price. As far as a general recommendation I would say yes but only to more dedicated fans to the genre.
